about: The writing brief's banned words and shapes (S/plans/839-writing-brief.md, 'Tone: documentation, not marketing'), as case-insensitive regular expressions, and exemptions: exact phrases, scoped to page ids, each with its reason. An exempted phrase is blanked before every word rule runs on that page. quotes exempts a quoted run of more than three words the same way.

banned.why: praise, unless it names the Quick start
a promise about time, unless a measured fact
no em dashes used as asides

exemptions.why: Students' code runs in Python on these pages; it is the language a teacher writes, not the machinery that runs it.
The page is about 3D models students can turn (#691); the site's MACHINERY list means a language model.
Python is the language of the code these pages show (the ready-made courses' code blocks, MTH1W's Coding pages); it is what a teacher writes, not the machinery that runs anything.
The name of SNC1W's own page in Tutorials, which shows programs for students to read; a page's name is quoted as the course has it.
Models is the name of a folder in the ready-made course CIA4U (its pages are economic models such as Supply and Demand); it is not a language model.

quotes.why: Obsidian's own name for a button in its trust question; the app's sentence (obsidianAddOnsForFigures.wording.settingFooter) quotes it the same way, and a teacher must match it on screen.

quotes.phrase: To access GitHub Education benefits, you need to be a currently employed educator at an accredited educational institution.
